claim_en: הלוא ("is it not?") written FULL with vav and aleph: the Ramah counts TWELVE plene in the Torah — "a Masorah for the whole Torah" — and the FIRST is here, opening the sin-at-the-door counsel. SNAPSHOT: exactly 12, first at 4:7.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 4:7 (Ramah; Sepharad books)
claim_en: אם תיטיב ("if you do well") — תיטיב written FULL with two yods, "one before the tet and one after" (Ramah). First token locked.
ואם לא תיטיב ("and if you do not do well") — the second תיטיב "likewise" full with both yods (Ramah). Second token locked.
ואליך תשוקתו ("and to you is its longing") — the FIRST tav carries a dagesh (doubling dot): the woman's sentence-word re-aimed at sin, its pointing noted at the letter.

דמי אחיך ("your brother's BLOODS") — the blood-word is PLURAL: "his blood and the blood of his descendants," or the many wounds. The chain answers the frozen unit's own [OPEN] plural-bloods flag; SNAPSHOT locks the plural construct form.
כל מצאי ("whoever finds ME will kill me" — Cain's fear) — the kaf is SOFT (no dagesh, the doubling dot): the kaf+qamatz sequence is contiguous in SNAPSHOT, no dot between.
כל מצאו ("whoever finds HIM" — the protection decree) — the kaf carries a dagesh (doubling dot): the fear-verse and the protection-verse form a soft/hard minimal pair one verse apart.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 4:13 (the spelling dispute)
claim_en: DISCREPANCY OBSERVATION — מנשוא ("than I can bear"): the authorities split — five (old books, the scribe Rabbi Meir, a Yerushalmi copy) read DEFECTIVE without vav; the Hilleli codex, the Sepharad books, the Ramah, and Or Torah ("this is principal") read PLENE. SNAPSHOT writes it DEFECTIVE (מנשא) — siding with the defective camp AGAINST Minchat Shai's final ruling. The check locks what SNAPSHOT reads; the dispute is the finding.
ויבא קין ("and Cain brought") — the precise books read qadma (a forward-leaning accent) on the bet; another manuscript reads differently. SNAPSHOT: qadma.
מבכרות ("of the firstlings of his flock") — the Ramah: first vav ABSENT, second vav PRESENT; "every other spelling of the firstborn-word in the Torah is doubly defective." SNAPSHOT letter-exact.

The famous gap — ויאמר קין אל הבל אחיו ("and Cain said to Abel his brother" — and nothing said): precise manuscripts have NO paragraph break (pisqa) mid-verse here; "the printer erred" in adding one; Maimonides and Meiri count no section here. SNAPSHOT carries no paragraph-break data at all — instrument gap.

check.note: SNAPSHOT has no petucha/setuma (open/closed paragraph) instrumentation — verses/words tables carry no break columns; variant-and-gap class

claim_en: קדמת עדן ("east of Eden") — Cain settles where his father was exiled (the 3:24 east), "and the eastern quarter is ever the refuge of murderers" (Deut 4:41, the refuge cities): the chain draws the unit's own east-of-Eden geography arrow and extends it to the manslayer law. SNAPSHOT: the construct קדמת ("east of") has exactly TWO Torah tokens, both in Eden's orbit — the rivers (2:14, east of Assyria) and the exile (4:16).

Our 4:2 carries TWO particles אֵת (et) - 'et his brother, et Abel' - and the doubled particle is read as counting people the verse does not name: each brother born with a twin sister. On this the four-children measure of the procreation obligation is argued, and Bar Kappara's rule that 'the addition exceeds the principal' opens here, Abel the addition born with two sisters.

THE CHAIN CATCHES A GENDER MISMATCH IN THE INK AND READS IT AS A GROWTH CURVE. At our 4:7 the noun חַטָּאת (chatat, 'sin') is feminine, yet the participle רֹבֵץ (rovetz, 'crouching') is MASCULINE - 'rovetzet is not written'. The reading: the inclination is weak as a female at first and strengthens as a male. Confirmed in the morphology at derivation: chatat is tagged feminine singular, rovetz masculine singular. Its FORM is separately disputed - Rav reads a fly between the two chambers of the heart, Shmuel a grain of wheat.

Our 4:7 conditional is read as a whole therapeutic program and as a law of legal FORM. THE PROGRAM: 'I created the evil inclination and I created TORAH AS ITS ANTIDOTE' - proof from this verse's 'if you do well'; not engaged, sin crouches; 'to you its desire' means its business is with you alone; and וְאַתָּה תִּמְשָׁל בּוֹ ('and you shall rule over it') is read as a PROMISE of mastery, not a hope. THE FORM: R. Meir's requirement that a legal condition be stated in both directions takes this verse's double formulation as its exhibit - so the machine's if-then-else operator carries the corpus's own condition-syntax law. And Antoninus taught Rebbi from this verse that the inclination rules from EMERGENCE, not formation - a ruling the chain canonized from a gentile's argument.

check.note: One conditional operator carrying a therapeutic reading and a law about the syntax of conditions.

claim_en: A CLAIM ABOUT THIS MACHINE'S OWN PARSE. Isi ben Yehudah censuses the verses of Scripture whose cut-point cannot be decided - and שְׂאֵת (se'et) of OUR 4:7 HEADS THE LIST. The tradition records that the verse cannot be parsed determinately: the word may close the preceding clause or open the following one. The unit's binary tree over 4:7 must therefore carry an undecidable-cut flag rather than assert a split.

check.note: The tradition's own record that this verse resists the very operation the parse layer performs. A constraint on the machine, not a finding about the world.

claim_en: THE EMPTY QUOTE, FILLED THREE WAYS. Our 4:8 reads 'and Cain SAID to his brother Abel' and then reports no words at all. The chain supplies three quarrels: the division of the world (land against movables - 'take off what you wear' / 'fly'); IN WHOSE DOMAIN THE TEMPLE WOULD STAND, reading 'the field' as the Temple mount, so the first murder is over the sanctuary's site; and a woman. Abel is read as the STRONGER - 'rose up' meaning Cain had been pinned and was released on a mercy-plea, then killed - and the weapon is disputed, stick against stone.

check.note: An operator whose speech payload is empty in the ink and supplied three ways by the chain.

source: Mishnah Sanhedrin 4:5; Bereshit Rabbah 22:9; Sanhedrin 37b:10; Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 4:9:1
claim_en: THE CAPITAL-COURT CROWN RESTS ON A PLURAL. דְּמֵי אָחִיךָ (demei achikha, 'the BLOODS of your brother', our 4:10) is written plural - confirmed in the morphology at derivation as a masculine PLURAL construct - and from that plural the court's standing warning to witnesses in capital cases is built: 'his blood and the blood of his descendants'. With it come the great rulings - that the first human was created SINGLE so that whoever destroys one life is as one who destroyed a whole world, and whoever sustains one life sustains a whole world. A textual variance is on the record: this seat reads 'a single life of Israel' where the Jerusalem Talmud seat reads simply 'a single life'.

source: Pesikta DeRav Kahana 24:11; Sanhedrin 37b:12; Vayikra Rabbah 10:5
claim_en: HALF THE DECREE IS REMITTED, AND THE INK SHOWS IT. The sentence at our 4:12 is נָע וָנָד (na va-nad, 'wandering AND roaming'), and Cain echoes both terms at 4:14 - but the settlement notice at 4:16 records him dwelling 'in the land of נוֹד (Nod)' with the first term GONE. Machine-checked at derivation: נָע stands in the Torah exactly twice, at 4:12 and 4:14, and נוֹד exactly once, at 4:16. The chain reads the dropped term as half the decree lifted, and gives three mechanisms for it across three seats - repentance remits half; exile itself atones for half; or repentance against prayer as a dispute.

Cain's plea at our 4:13 carries THREE recorded readings, held dual-track: REPROACH - 'You bear worlds, and not my sin?'; CONFESSION - 'my sin is greater than my father's; his was a light command, mine is bloodshed'; and DEMAND - 'is my sin greater than that of the six hundred thousand whom You will forgive?'. The departure at 4:16 is likewise read three ways, one of them JOYFUL - and on that reading the meeting with Adam follows, where Cain says 'I repented and it was settled', and Adam strikes his own face: 'SUCH IS THE POWER OF REPENTANCE AND I DID NOT KNOW' - then composes the Sabbath psalm as a psalm of repentance.

check.note: Three readings of one plea, carried without merger.

claim_en: THE SUSPENDED SENTENCE IS DISCHARGED IN A LATER UNIT. Our 4:15 sets a seven-generations clause on anyone who kills Cain, and the machine leaves it open. R. Levi in the name of Reish Lakish closes it: the יְקוּם ('the standing substance' swept away at Genesis 7:23) is CAIN - he hung in abeyance until the Flood came and swept him away. A demand this unit files is satisfied five units downstream.

check.note: An open clause in this unit discharged at a named later verse - a cross-unit demand and its receipt.

source: Pesikta DeRav Kahana 9:4; Sifra, Shemini, Mekhilta DeMiluim II 31
claim_en: From the acceptance of Abel's offering at our 4:4 the chain opens the census of THE PURSUED - 'Abel was pursued by Cain, and God seeks the pursued', extending even to a righteous man who pursues a wicked one - and derives the SPECIES rule of the altar from it: bring before Me only from the pursued, the ox, the sheep and the goat, which is given as the stated rationale of Leviticus 22:27. Rebbi separately reads this offering as the liturgy's benchmark: 'as in former years - the YEARS OF ABEL, when idolatry was not yet in the world'.

check.note: An offering-species law and a liturgical benchmark read off one acceptance operator.

claim_en: ABEL'S FATS PROVE THE PEACE-OFFERING ARM. Did the sons of Noah offer peace-offerings? The yes arm rides this verse's of-their-fats — what has its fat offered but not all of it? — with the no arm recorded beside. Filed F-167, auto-seated (round 38, the altar-before-Sinai block).
